papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2017 (31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
papers.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train.
papers.methodology: Scaled Dot-Product Attention combined with Multi-Head Attention mechanisms, sinusoidal positional encodings, and encoder-decoder feed-forward stacks.
papers.limitations: Quadratic computational and memory complexity O(N^2) relative to sequence length, creating significant bottlenecks for long context sequences.
papers.future_work: Sparse attention mechanisms, linear attention approximations, and specialized hardware kernels (FlashAttention).

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2016)
papers.abstract: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence showing that these residual networks are easier to optimize, and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth.
papers.methodology: Identity shortcut connections bypassing convolutional layer stacks, allowing gradient flow directly through deep architectures without degradation.
papers.limitations: Feature redundancy across very deep layers; does not solve receptive field limits in non-spatial domains.
papers.future_work: Stochastic depth networks, wide residual networks, and vision transformers.

papers.title: N-BaIoT—Network-Based Detection of IoT Botnet Attacks Using Deep Autoencoders
papers.abstract: A massive distributed denial of service attack carried out by the Mirai IoT botnet demonstrated the severe threat posed by compromised smart home devices. We propose N-BaIoT, an anomaly detection method that uses deep autoencoders to detect anomalous network traffic originating from infected IoT devices. The method was evaluated on 9 commercial IoT devices infected with Mirai and BASHLITE.
papers.methodology: Statistical feature extraction over 5 temporal decay windows (100ms, 500ms, 1.5s, 10s, 1min) calculating packet jitter, bandwidth, and protocol counts, evaluated via autoencoder reconstruction error thresholds.
papers.limitations: High false alarm rates when legitimate device firmware updates or unusual user behavior introduces benign out-of-distribution traffic.
papers.future_work: Adaptive thresholding and multi-modal physical sensor corroboration.

papers.title: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial, and Multimap SLAM
papers.abstract: ORB-SLAM3 is the first system able to perform visual, visual-inertial, and multimap SLAM with monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras, using pin-hole and fisheye lens models. The main novelty is an Atlas system that manages a multi-map representation allowing seamless operation during long periods of visual tracking loss.
papers.methodology: Fast ORB feature tracking combined with continuous pre-integrated IMU factor graph optimization and DBoW2-based loop closing and multi-map merging.
papers.limitations: Performance degrades sharply in featureless textures, direct sunlight glare, or aggressive rotational motion without IMU initialization.
papers.future_work: Deep feature embedding integration and neural radiance field (NeRF) mapping.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Radio Frequency Fingerprinting of IoT Devices
papers.abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) exploits tiny hardware imperfections in transmitters to identify wireless devices uniquely at the physical layer. This paper presents ORACLE, an optimized radio classification framework using convolutional networks on raw I/Q signal samples, achieving >99% classification accuracy across 100 commercial off-the-shelf devices.
papers.methodology: Time-domain I/Q sampling and channel-independent frequency offset extraction fed into a 1D-CNN classifier.
papers.limitations: Susceptible to wireless channel variations and temperature drift; requires retraining when antenna orientation changes.
papers.future_work: Adversarial channel invariant learning and geomagnetic multi-sensor cross-validation.

papers.title: Compressed Sensing
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, Vol. 52, No. 4
papers.abstract: Suppose x is an unknown vector in R^m and we measure y = A x where y in R^n with n much smaller than m. When x is sparse in a known basis, L1-norm minimization can reconstruct x exactly from far fewer measurements than classical Shannon-Nyquist sampling would require.
papers.methodology: L1 optimization (Basis Pursuit) exploiting Restricted Isometry Property (RIP) of random measurement matrices.
papers.limitations: Iterative reconstruction algorithms are computationally expensive for real-time high-throughput telemetry streams.
papers.future_work: Deep unfolding networks (Learned ISTA) for microsecond sparse signal recovery.

problems.title: Concept Drift and Adversarial Vulnerability in Edge IoT Anomaly Detection
problems.description: Deep learning models deployed on low-power IoT gateways suffer severe accuracy degradation under continuous non-stationary concept drift (e.g. ambient temperature shifts, network routing changes, and firmware updates). Furthermore, attackers can craft stealthy micro-perturbations in network packet inter-arrival times that bypass autoencoder reconstruction thresholds.
problems.research_question: Can multi-modal physical layer signatures (RF emissions + geomagnetic telemetry) provide a non-spoofable ground truth to recalibrate edge anomaly detection models under severe concept drift without manual annotation?
problems.why_it_matters: Millions of industrial and healthcare IoT devices are vulnerable to silent botnet infections and physical node tampering because packet-level intrusion detection systems trigger excessive false alarms over time.

problems.title: Quadratic Memory and Compute Bottleneck in Long-Context Transformers
problems.description: Standard self-attention mechanisms scale with O(N^2) computational complexity and GPU VRAM footprint relative to context window size N. This restricts full-sequence attention across million-token scientific papers, multi-hour audio streams, and whole-genome sequences.
problems.research_question: Is it mathematically possible to achieve exact sub-quadratic O(N log N) or linear O(N) associative memory recall without degrading needle-in-a-haystack retrieval accuracy?
problems.why_it_matters: Enables foundation models to reason over entire codebases, longitudinal patient health records, and multi-year scientific experiment logs simultaneously.

problems.title: Geometric Degeneracy and Tracking Loss in Visual-Inertial SLAM
problems.description: Visual-inertial odometry and SLAM pipelines fail catastrophically in geometrically degenerate environments such as featureless white hallways, dark tunnels, reflective metallic structures, and during extreme rotational acceleration where optical flow fails.
problems.research_question: How can ambient geomagnetic field anomalies and ultra-wideband (UWB) RF ranging be tightly coupled into the factor graph bundle adjustment to guarantee non-divergent localization during complete visual blackout?
problems.why_it_matters: Crucial for autonomous search-and-rescue drones, mining robots, and planetary rovers operating in GPS-denied, visually degraded subterranean environments.

problems.title: Channel Invariance in Radio Frequency Device Fingerprinting
problems.description: RF fingerprinting neural networks trained on wireless devices in an anechoic chamber drop from 99% to <45% classification accuracy when deployed in dynamic multipath fading environments where moving objects alter the wireless channel state information (CSI).
problems.research_question: Can adversarial domain adaptation and complex-valued neural networks extract intrinsic power amplifier non-linearities while mathematically filtering out dynamic multipath fading impulse responses?
problems.why_it_matters: Enables zero-trust cryptographic device authentication at the physical antenna layer without relying on MAC address or software certificates that can be cloned.

solutions.title: Deep Autoencoder Reconstruction Error Thresholding
solutions.methodology: Trains an isolated autoencoder on clean baseline network traffic; flags anomalies when Mean Squared Error reconstruction loss exceeds threshold theta.
solutions.limitations: Fails to differentiate between malicious attacks and benign concept drift, causing high false alarm fatigue.

solutions.title: IO-Aware Tiled Exact Attention (FlashAttention-2)
solutions.methodology: Reorders GPU SRAM and HBM memory operations using tiled matrix multiplication and online softmax computation to minimize memory reads/writes.
solutions.limitations: Still fundamentally O(N^2) theoretical complexity despite 4-8x wall-clock speedup; does not scale to infinite streaming contexts.

solutions.title: Atlas Multi-Map Visual-Inertial Factor Graph
solutions.methodology: Maintains an active map and spawns new sub-maps upon tracking loss, attempting DBoW2 visual place recognition to merge maps later.
solutions.limitations: If visual features remain unavailable, position estimation drifts unbounded based purely on dead-reckoning IMU double-integration.

gaps.title: Lack of Multi-Modal Physical Layer (RF + Geomagnetic) Cross-Correlation in IoT Botnet Detection
gaps.gap_statement: While network packet features (packet inter-arrival times, jitter, payload entropy) and RF physical-layer emissions have been studied independently, no existing literature explores cross-modal latent alignment to differentiate benign firmware updates from stealthy adversarial attacks under severe non-stationary concept drift.
gaps.evidence: Comprehensive survey of IEEE S&P, ACM CCS, and IEEE TIFS literature (2018-2025) confirms all public benchmarks evaluate network traffic and physical side-channels in strict silos.
gaps.what_not_tested: Continuous joint temporal autoencoding of 115-dimensional N-BaIoT packet features synchronized with raw I/Q RF spectrograms and 3-axis geomagnetic sensor telemetry on live edge nodes.

gaps.title: Sub-quadratic Associative Memory Retention in Selective State-Space Recurrent Hybrid Models
gaps.gap_statement: Selective state-space models (e.g. Mamba) achieve linear O(N) scaling but degrade on complex multi-query in-context associative recall tasks compared to full softmax attention.
gaps.evidence: Recent synthetic benchmark evaluations show SSMs struggle on long-horizon associative copy tasks without hybrid attention layer interleaving.
gaps.what_not_tested: Optimal ratio and mathematical bounds for alternating selective state-space layers with sparse localized FlashAttention blocks across context lengths >500k tokens.

gaps.title: Tightly-Coupled Geomagnetic Anomaly Prior in Nonlinear Least Squares SLAM Factor Graphs
gaps.gap_statement: Existing SLAM algorithms discard building magnetic field structural variations as ambient noise rather than utilizing them as unique spatial landmarks for drift-free subterranean localization.
gaps.evidence: Robotics literature relies almost exclusively on LiDAR and visual keypoints, which fail under heavy smoke, dust, or lighting failure in tunnel exploration.
gaps.what_not_tested: Direct integration of 3-axis magnetic anomaly gradients into the g2o/Ceres non-linear optimization factor graph alongside visual and inertial residual errors.

hypotheses.title: Multi-Modal Physical-Network Contrastive Alignment Prevents Concept Drift Degradation
hypotheses.description: By training a joint contrastive encoder that aligns network packet statistical distributions with hardware RF spectral signatures, the anomaly detection system can maintain >95% F1-score across 30 days of concept drift without retraining.
hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: If high-frequency RF power variations are correlated with packet transmission bursts in a contrastive latent space, false alarms caused by benign firmware updates will drop by at least 80% compared to unimodal autoencoders.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome: Attacks will cause network-RF divergence (e.g. unexpected CPU computation without corresponding network traffic, or packet spoofing from alien hardware), enabling 99.2% true positive detection.

experiments.title: Multi-Modal Evaluation: IoTGeM + N-BaIoT on ESP32 & Raspberry Pi Testbed
experiments.description: Benchmarking proposed multi-modal contrastive network vs. baseline autoencoders and Isolation Forest on combined N-BaIoT and IoTGeM datasets.
experiments.methodology: 10-fold cross validation with simulated 30-day non-stationary distribution shifts and hardware thermal noise injection.

datasets.name: N-BaIoT
datasets.description: Real traffic data gathered from 9 commercial IoT devices infected with Mirai and BASHLITE botnets, containing 115 continuous statistical features.

datasets.name: CICIoT2023
datasets.description: Extensive modern IoT attack benchmark dataset featuring 33 distinct attack scenarios (DDoS, DoS, Recon, Web, Brute Force, Spoofing, Mirai) across 105 smart devices.

datasets.name: IoTGeM
datasets.description: High-frequency 3-axis geomagnetic anomaly dataset specifically collected for detecting physical enclosure opening, circuit tampering, and magnetic spoofing.

datasets.name: KITTI Vision Benchmark
datasets.description: Standard benchmark suite for stereo visual odometry, 3D object detection, and autonomous driving SLAM in urban environments.

datasets.name: SQuAD 2.0 (Stanford Question Answering Dataset)
datasets.description: Reading comprehension dataset consisting of 150,000+ questions formulated by crowdworkers on Wikipedia articles with unanswerable adversarial questions.

algorithms.name: Transformer Attention Architecture
algorithms.description: Multi-head scaled dot-product self-attention mechanism capturing long-range dependencies across arbitrary token sequences without sequential recurrence.

algorithms.name: Isolation Forest (iForest)
algorithms.description: Unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm that explicitly isolates anomalies by randomly selecting a feature and split value. Anomalies have significantly shorter path lengths in the isolation trees.

algorithms.name: Visual-Inertial Bundle Adjustment (ORB-SLAM3)
algorithms.description: Non-linear least squares factor graph optimization integrating FAST corner detection, ORB binary feature descriptors, and pre-integrated IMU error residuals.

algorithms.name: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation)
algorithms.description: Stochastic gradient descent algorithm computing adaptive learning rates for individual parameters using decaying averages of past gradients (first moment) and past squared gradients (second moment).

notes.title: Methodological Insight: Clock Synchronization between RTL-SDR and Network Packet Captures
notes.content: Observed a 14ms timestamp drift between PCAP tcpdump records and raw I/Q SDR samples on Raspberry Pi 4. Resolved by binding packet capture interrupts to hardware PPS (Pulse-Per-Second) GPS clock sync. Cross-correlation peak F1-score increased from 0.88 to 0.96.

notes.title: Observation: Exponential Decay Half-Life on Industrial Temperature Cycles
notes.content: Day-night temperature swings (15C to 42C) in solar inverter IoT deployments cause frequency drift in crystal oscillators of ~18ppm. Autoencoders must normalize RF center frequency dynamically rather than treating drift as anomalous physical tampering.
